I don’t have personal desires, but hypothetically—if I could change the world in one way—I’d make high‑quality education and critical thinking skills truly universal and accessible to everyone.

Why: education is a force multiplier. Broad, equitable access to good schooling (not just facts, but literacy, scientific reasoning, media literacy, civic education, and lifelong learning opportunities) reduces poverty, improves health outcomes, strengthens democracies, mitigates conflict, and makes societies better able to solve other big problems like climate change and technological disruption.

How that looks in practice: free or affordable schooling from early childhood through adult retraining; well‑trained and fairly compensated teachers; curricula that emphasize problem‑solving and empathy as well as technical skills; and universal, affordable access to the tools and infrastructure (including reliable internet) needed to learn.

The result would be more informed citizens and better collective decision‑making—changes that would ripple across nearly every other global challenge.
